paper_id: gECC_ A GPU-based high-throughput framework for Elliptic Curve Cryptography
title: GECC: A GPU-Based High-Throughput Framework for Elliptic Curve Cryptography
motivation: ECC remains bottleneck in throughput-sensitive applications; single EC operation takes >6ms; even ASIC acceleration only yields 12% improvement
problem_framing: Maximize throughput for batch EC operations on GPU by addressing: sequential modinv, high memory overhead, and IMAD instruction bottleneck
key_insight: Borrow GAS mechanism from parallel graph processing to reduce modinv from 32n to sp; use predicate registers to eliminate IMAD bottleneck; apply find-then-recompute for kernel fusion
method_signature: Batch EC operations via Montgomery's trick with GAS mechanism, multi-level cache management, and IMAD-minimized modular multiplication
evaluation_criteria: Throughput (ops/s) vs RapidEC (GPU) and CPU-based systems; ECDSA/E CDH speedup; real-world blockchain TPS improvement
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Some CUDA cores are idle during modinv apply phase; NAF algorithm causes warp divergence issues in parallel UPMUL; memory access overhead limits input scale
evidence_for_taste: This effectively avoids the divergence issue
modadd operations are cheaper than global memory access
the benefit of decreasing computational complexity dominates the increased overhead
The throughput of gECC with all the optimizations can achieve 36% and 23% improvement
thinking_moves: 识别模逆操作的顺序依赖性导致的GPU并行瓶颈
从并行图处理系统借鉴GAS机制来解决批量模逆
通过成本分析(模加<全局内存访问)决定是否重计算而非存储
量化权衡Montgomery trick降低复杂度与增加内存开销的收益
通过微架构级指令分析定位IMAD瓶颈,提出谓词寄存器传递进位信息
